info.description:
## Overview

Use this API specification, as a secondary care provider, to build an API that the Wayfinder Direct Integration service can use to manage appointments for a patient using FHIR R4 (4.0.1).

This specification contains the following operations:
* Search for appointments, including supported `_include` results.
* Search for slots by status and time window, with service filtering and related-resource inclusions.
* Get, create, update, patch and delete an appointment.
* Retrieve the server capability statement using `/metadata`.

FHIR APIs are RESTful APIs that follow specific rules. In particular:
* resource names are capitalised and singular, for example `/Appointment` not `/appointments`
* array names are singular, for example `entry` not `entries` for FHIR bundle entries
* data items that are country-specific and thus not included in the FHIR global base resources are usually wrapped in an `extension` object

## Relationship to BaRS

This Direct Integration API is based on and aligned with the Booking and Referral Standard (BaRS). It focuses on the Appointment, Slot and metadata operations described in this specification.

BaRS is the definitive reference for the standard, including its requirements, resource definitions and implementation guidance. This specification supplements that guidance for direct integration; it does not replace or redefine BaRS. If this specification differs from BaRS, the BaRS standard takes precedence, and the difference should be treated as a limitation to be resolved.

Refer to the [BaRS implementation guide](https://simplifier.net/guide/nhsbookingandreferralstandard) for the authoritative guidance. Alignment with BaRS does not, by itself, establish that this specification has been formally assessed or approved as conformant.

## Who can use this API standard

You can only use this API standard if you are integrating a secondary care booking system with the Wayfinder Direct Integration service.

As a secondary care provider, you will also need to use the [Patient Care Aggregator Record Service API](https://digital.nhs.uk/developer/api-catalogue/patient-care-aggregator-record-service/patient-care-aggregator-record-service-api) to let the Patient Care Aggregator know which patients you have appointments for.

## Status

This API specification is in **draft / experimental** status. It is available for review and prototyping and might be subject to breaking changes. The server CapabilityStatement returned by `/metadata` reports `status: draft` and `experimental: true`.

## Technology

This API standard is [RESTful](https://digital.nhs.uk/developer/guides-and-documentation/api-technologies-at-nhs-digital#basic-rest). It conforms to the [FHIR](https://digital.nhs.uk/developer/guides-and-documentation/api-technologies-at-nhs-digital#fhir) global standard for health care data exchange, specifically to [FHIR R4 (v4.0.1)](https://hl7.org/fhir/r4/). It includes some country-specific FHIR extensions, which have been built against [FHIR UK Core](https://digital.nhs.uk/services/fhir-uk-core).

## Network access

This API is available on the internet and, indirectly, on the [Health and Social Care Network (HSCN)](https://digital.nhs.uk/services/health-and-social-care-network). For more details, see [Network access for APIs](https://digital.nhs.uk/developer/guides-and-documentation/network-access-for-apis).

## Non-functional requirements

Your API must be a gold service, meaning it is operational and supported 24 hours a day, 365 days a year. For more details, see [service levels](https://digital.nhs.uk/developer/guides-and-documentation/reference-guide#service-levels).

Your endpoint must be capable of:
* responding to requests within 400ms (at the 95th percentile)
* a throughput of at least 60 transactions per second

Diagnostic logging requirements:
* all requests must be logged for diagnostic purposes
* log records must include the `X-Correlation-Id`
* personally identifiable and clinical information must be omitted from logs in production
* log records must be held for a minimum of 90 days

## Security and authentication

This prototype supports two alternative authentication modes on every operation, including `/metadata`: patient-based, user-restricted access through NHS login and NHS API Platform token exchange; or application-based, application-restricted access through NHS API Platform client credentials with a signed JWT client assertion. Supply one API Platform bearer access token for the selected mode. Applications must be onboarded and authorised for that mode. This is the prototype's security profile; BaRS remains the definitive reference for the underlying standard.

### Patient-based authentication flow

Register the application separately with NHS login and NHS API Platform and enable access to this API in the chosen environment.

1. Authenticate the patient using the NHS login OpenID Connect authorisation-code flow and validate the returned ID token.
2. Exchange that ID token at the NHS API Platform token endpoint, authenticating the application with a signed client assertion.
3. Send the resulting API Platform access token as `Authorization: Bearer <access_token>` on every API request, including `/metadata`.

Use `https://int.api.service.nhs.uk/oauth2/token` for integration testing and `https://api.service.nhs.uk/oauth2/token` for production. Follow the [NHS token-exchange guidance](https://digital.nhs.uk/developer/guides-and-documentation/security-and-authorisation/user-restricted-restful-apis-nhs-login-separate-authentication-and-authorisation) for request parameters, client assertions, token refresh and environment pairing.

The bearer credential for this API is the exchanged access token. Do not send an NHS login ID token, NHS login access token or client assertion as this API's bearer credential.

### Patient identity and verification

NHS login uses `openid` for authentication; request the approved `profile` scope when an NHS number is needed for patient matching. Validate identity claims and the returned verification level using the [NHS login OIDC guidance](https://nhsconnect.github.io/nhslogin/oidc-login-flow/) and [scopes and claims guidance](https://nhsconnect.github.io/nhslogin/scopes-and-claims/).

Prototype policy: patient-based appointment access requires high identity verification (P9). Configure the accepted authentication vectors during onboarding; do not infer adequate assurance merely from a successful sign-in. See [NHS login verification guidance](https://nhsconnect.github.io/nhslogin/step-up-p5-p9/).

### Application-based authentication flow

Register the application and its public key with NHS API Platform and enable application-restricted access to this API in the chosen environment.

1. Generate a signed JWT client assertion using the application's private key.
2. POST to the environment's token endpoint using `application/x-www-form-urlencoded`, with `grant_type=client_credentials`, `client_assertion_type=urn:ietf:params:oauth:client-assertion-type:jwt-bearer` and `client_assertion=<signed application client assertion>`.
3. Send the returned access token as `Authorization: Bearer <access_token>` on each API request, including `/metadata`.

Use the integration or production token URL given above. Follow the [NHS application-restricted authentication guidance](https://digital.nhs.uk/developer/guides-and-documentation/security-and-authorisation/application-restricted-restful-apis-signed-jwt-authentication) for signing requirements and token renewal. This mode does not authenticate a patient through NHS login; the patient P9 requirement does not apply to application credentials.

### Token validation and authentication context

The API gateway must validate the API Platform access token, its authorisation for this API and its authentication mode. It must convey the authenticated application, mode and, for patient-based access, patient identity and assurance to the receiving service through a trusted channel. The receiving service must reject untrusted identity context. Do not assume an access token is a locally decodable JWT. Never select application-based access merely because patient identity is missing or an organisation header is present; reject incomplete or invalid authentication context.

### Organisation header

`NHSD-End-User-Organisation` is optional in the OpenAPI parameter definition because its requirement depends on the authenticated mode. It MUST be provided for application-based authentication and SHOULD NOT be provided for patient-based authentication, including requests to `/metadata`. For application access, the receiving service must validate the decoded organisation identifier against the organisations the authenticated application is permitted to represent. Supplying this header does not itself establish authority. For patient access, its presence must not change the authentication mode or broaden access.

### Patient authorisation — prototype policy

For patient-based access, every appointment request must be authorised against the authenticated patient's local record:

* Searches return only that patient's appointments. Supplied identifiers and demographic filters must not broaden access to another patient.
* Reads, updates, patches and deletes require the appointment to belong to that patient.
* Creation must bind the appointment to that patient. Updates and patches must not reassign it to another patient.
* Included resources must be authorised for disclosure in the context of the permitted appointment.
* Acting for another patient requires a separately defined delegated-access policy; this prototype does not grant that access.

Authentication does not automatically permit every operation. The receiving service must also enforce its appointment-management rules and application permissions. Routing, software, organisation and practitioner headers provide context, not proof of patient identity.

### Application authorisation — prototype policy

For application-based access, the receiving service must authorise each operation against the authenticated application's permissions, validated organisation context and the requested patient and appointment. Application authentication does not grant unrestricted access to all patients.

* Searches and included resources must be restricted to records the application and represented organisation are authorised to access. Patient identifiers and demographic filters select records; they do not prove authority to access them.
* Reads, updates, patches and deletes require permission for the target appointment and patient.
* Creation requires permission to create an appointment for the specified patient. Updates and patches must not bypass patient or organisation access restrictions.
* Enforce appointment-management rules and record the authenticated application and validated organisation in the audit trail. Any supplied practitioner context must be checked against the receiving service's policy and does not itself authenticate a practitioner.

### Authentication and authorisation failures

Return `401` for missing, invalid or expired API credentials, with a `WWW-Authenticate: Bearer` challenge. Return `403` when valid credentials lack sufficient permissions, organisation or patient access, or required patient assurance. Return an OperationOutcome without disclosing another patient's details. For application-based requests, return `400` with an OperationOutcome when the required organisation header is missing or malformed, and `403` when the application is not permitted to represent the supplied organisation. OAuth token-endpoint errors follow the linked NHS guidance and are outside this API's paths.

### Deployment

This specification defines the intended security contract. API Platform configuration for both modes, token validation, organisation validation and mode-specific authorisation must be implemented and enabled before deployment. NHS login onboarding and patient identity verification are additionally required for patient-based access. Listing the NHS API Platform environment URLs does not imply that this API is already available on NHS API Platform.

## Errors

Error responses use HTTP status codes and the OperationOutcome structure defined in this specification.

get.description:
### Returns the target endpoints CapabilityStatement 

The sender must initially request the Receiver's [CapabilityStatement](https://www.hl7.org/fhir/capabilitystatement.html) (GET /metadata) to establish how to interact with the receivers API (its capabilities). If the receiver does not support BaRS functionality the BaRS API will provide an error response to indicate this and the sender will pursue an alternative workflow. 

A receiver may only implement a subset of the functionality within the standard and the CapabilityStatement will make this clear to a sender. 

What is returned is a server level response to indicate what functionality the target API supports and how to interact with it. This includes its Version, Security, Endpoints and their associated parameters as well as which MessageDefinitions are supported.

Any given endpoint will describe its full capabilities as a client and as a server in response. As the Sender and Receiver roles are interchangeable in certain Application Workflows, all capabilities should be described. 

The BaRS proxy will also respond with its own CapabilityStatement, which can be used as an example, by calling this endpoint and omitting the NHSD-Target-Identifier header.

security.description: Supports patient-based authentication through NHS login and NHS API Platform token exchange (NHSLoginPatientAccess), or application-based authentication through NHS API Platform client credentials with a signed JWT client assertion (NHSApplicationAccess). Patient-based access requires patient-level authorisation and P9 verification. Application-based access requires NHSD-End-User-Organisation and authorisation for the application, represented organisation and requested records.

searchParam.name: _id
searchParam.documentation: The FHIR logical id of a single Appointment. Optional; when supplied the search returns the matching Appointment (with any requested _include resources) in a searchset Bundle. A plain read is also available via GET /Appointment/{id}.

searchParam.name: patient:identifier
searchParam.documentation: The patient's NHS number (system must be https://fhir.nhs.uk/Id/nhs-number).

searchParam.name: patient:name
searchParam.documentation: The patient's name. Used in conjunction with birthdate and postcode to ensure a unique match.

searchParam.name: patient:birthdate
searchParam.documentation: The patient's date of birth. Used in conjunction with name and postcode to ensure a unique match.

searchParam.name: patient:address-postalcode
searchParam.documentation: The patient's home address postcode. Used in conjunction with name and date of birth to ensure a unique match.

searchParam.name: status
searchParam.documentation:
Status values that need to be considered for filter. 

If attempting to filter by multiple status' they must be separated with commas as opposed to defining the query parameter twice as defined in [FHIR Guidance](https://hl7.org/fhir/search.html#combining)

For example "GET [base]/Slot?status=free,busy".

searchParam.name: start
searchParam.documentation:
Slot start date/time (yyyy-mm-ddThh:mm:ss+00:00).
To search for time windows within which Slots must start, use "greater than" and "less than" searching.

For example "GET [base]/Slot?start=ge2022-03-01T12:00:00+00:00&start=le2022-03-01T13:30:00+00:00". 
The definition of the time window within which Slots are requested is provided by using this parameter twice.
The values must include an offset indicating UTC in the [FHIR dateTime format](https://www.hl7.org/fhir/datatypes.html#primitive). This is the case for all dateTimes in the BaRS standard.

get.description:
### Returns appointments for a specified patient
Use this endpoint to get all appointments for a given patient. All appointments for the specified patient at the specified target endpoint will be returned in a FHIR searchset Bundle containing Appointment resources. 

If a sender wants to cancel a particular appointment, they must perform a read first, comparing and amending the details prior to performing the update.


### Appointment inclusion / exclusion rules
This is a patient-facing route (appointments are surfaced to the citizen, e.g. via the NHS App). Receivers MUST filter the result set so that only appointments the patient is permitted to see are returned. The following rules apply:

* **NHS in England only** — only include appointments for care settings within the NHS in England.
* **Excluded patients (Trust flag)** — exclude appointments for patients flagged, from within the Trust, as not permitted access via the NHS App.
* **Excluded patients (PDS sensitive/restricted)** — exclude appointments for patients whose PDS (Personal Demographics Service) record is flagged sensitive/restricted.
* **Under-16** — exclude patients under 16 years of age (see decision note below).

**How exclusions are surfaced (no disclosure):** where appointments are withheld by the England-only, Trust-flag or PDS-sensitive rules — or where the patient genuinely has no appointments — the endpoint MUST return the empty happy path: HTTP `200` with a FHIR searchset Bundle whose `total` is `0`. A withheld record MUST be indistinguishable from a patient who simply has no appointments; the response MUST NOT reveal that a patient is excluded, sensitive or restricted.

> **REVIEW / DECISION NEEDED (under-16):** The Wayfinder standard models the under-16 case as an explicit `403 UNDER_16_DENIED` (see the 4XX error table), which is *inconsistent* with the silent empty-`200` treatment used for the PDS-sensitive and Trust-flag exclusions above. Returning a distinct 403 discloses that an excluded record exists. Decision required: either (a) treat under-16 as a silent empty `200 total:0` for consistency and non-disclosure, or (b) retain the explicit `403 UNDER_16_DENIED`. This must be resolved before the exclusion behaviour is final.

> **NOTE (overlap with authorisation):** these are *eligibility/business* exclusions applied by the Receiver to the result set, and are distinct from the authentication/authorisation checks in the Security section (which govern whether the caller may access the patient at all). Both apply: a request can be fully authorised yet still return an empty `200` because of these exclusion rules.

post.description:
Create a single Appointment resource.

**Response status — 200, not 201:** a successful create returns `200` with the created Appointment in the response body. `201 Created` is intentionally **not** used because the API does not return a `Location` header pointing to the newly created resource. This is in line with BaRS, where the created/updated resource (including its server-assigned `id`) is returned in the body and the client reads the `id` from there rather than from a `Location` header.

Patient access: the receiving service must authorise this operation for the authenticated patient and restrict all returned or modified resources accordingly. See the patient-authorisation policy in the API overview.

Application access: the receiving service must authorise this operation for the authenticated application and validated organisation. NHSD-End-User-Organisation MUST be supplied. See the application-authorisation policy in the API overview.

200.description: Appointment created successfully. The created Appointment (including its server-assigned `id`) is returned in the response body. Note: `201 Created` is not used and no `Location` header is returned — read the resource `id` from the body. This is in line with BaRS.

get.description:
### Get available slots

A call to Slots is for querying a target endpoint for suitable slots to book a new Appointment into for a patient. 
A request for slots support various filter parameters but requires the service identifier, slot status(es) and a timeframe to limit the search. 

As documented in the [NHS Booking Standard](https://developer.nhs.uk/apis/uec-appointments/fs_slotmanagement.html), a receiver assigns the service identifier to groups of slots, under a schedule, which ties schedules together for a particular service.

Direct Integration access: this operation supports the patient-based and application-based authentication modes defined in the API overview. Apply the existing mode-specific organisation-header requirements. Authorise access to the requested service and restrict returned slots and included resources to information the authenticated caller is permitted to view. Slot availability must not disclose another patient's identity or appointment details.

parameters.name: status
parameters.description:
Status values that need to be considered for filter. 

If attempting to filter by multiple status' they must be separated with commas as opposed to defining the query parameter twice as defined in [FHIR Guidance](https://hl7.org/fhir/search.html#combining)

For example "GET [base]/Slot?status=free,busy".

parameters.name: start
parameters.description:
Slot start date/time (yyyy-mm-ddThh:mm:ss+00:00).
To search for time windows within which Slots must start, use "greater than" and "less than" searching.

For example "GET [base]/Slot?start=ge2022-03-01T12:00:00+00:00&start=le2022-03-01T13:30:00+00:00". 
The definition of the time window within which Slots are requested is provided by using this parameter twice.
The values must include an offset indicating UTC in the [FHIR dateTime format](https://www.hl7.org/fhir/datatypes.html#primitive). This is the case for all dateTimes in the BaRS standard.

parameters.name: Schedule.actor:HealthcareService
parameters.description: A single service ID can be provided to indicate the service for which appointment slots are returned for.

parameters.name: _include
parameters.description:
Inclusions that drive the rescusive depth of the search. There is a minimum of the following _include parameters required for current Applications.
* Slot:schedule
* Schedule:actor:HealthcareService

**Note**: Both _include and _revinclude share the same syntax - up to three components, separated by colon characters (:). 
Unlike search queries, this is not a FHIRPath expression

The full list of applicable _includes are shown below. If any cannot be honored the Receiver will respond, ignoring the unsupported _include(s), with the url reflecting this omission in the responses Bundle.link.url. 

|Expression | Inclusion     |Description|
|-------    |--------       |-------- |
| Slot:schedule                    | Schedule           | Include Schedule Resources referenced within the  Slot Resources|
| Schedule:actor:Practitioner      | Practitioner       | Include Practitioner Resources referenced within the  Schedule Resources|
| Schedule:actor:PractitionerRole  | PractitionerRole   | Include Practitioner Role Resources referenced within the  Schedule Resources |
| Schedule:actor:HealthcareService | HealthcareService  | Include HealthcareService Resources referenced within the  Schedule Resources|
| HealthcareService:providedBy     | ProvidedBy         | Include Organization Resources referenced within the  HealthcareService Resources|
| HealthcareService:location       | Location           | Include Location Resources referenced within the  HealthcareService Resources|

200.description: Success. A full example of a Slot Searchset response can be found [here](  https://simplifier.net/NHSBookingandReferrals/777a156c-af3c-4748-a8a3-7e95e4b0df9a-duplicate-2).

RequestingOrganisation_HParam.name: NHSD-End-User-Organisation
RequestingOrganisation_HParam.description:
Requesting Organization described in an object based on a FHIR 'Organization' resource (Standard Base64 encoded JSON).

This header is optional in the OpenAPI parameter definition because its requirement depends on the authenticated mode:
* For application-based (B2B) authentication it MUST be provided, and the receiving service must validate the decoded organisation identifier against the organisations the authenticated application is permitted to represent.
* For patient-based authentication it is not required and SHOULD NOT be provided (including requests to `/metadata`); its presence must not change the authentication mode or broaden access.

Supplying this header does not itself establish authority. In the example given an ODS code and the Organisation name is provided. Other identifiers are permitted if required.

**Example object before encoding** 
  ```json
  {
    "resourceType": "Organization",
    "identifier": [
      {
        "value": "A1001",
        "system": "https://fhir.nhs.uk/Id/ods-organization-code"
      }
    ],
    "name": "My service provider name"
  }

AppointmentInclude_QParam.name: _include
AppointmentInclude_QParam.description:
Inclusions that drive the recursive depth of the search. Use this to ask the Receiver to return additional resources referenced by the Appointment(s), in the same response Bundle, rather than the sender having to perform separate follow-up reads.

**Note**: _include shares the same syntax as _revinclude - up to three components, separated by colon characters (:). Unlike search queries, this is not a FHIRPath expression.

The parameter can be repeated to request more than one inclusion on the same request, allowing a full chain of related resources (for example Appointment -> Slot -> Schedule -> HealthcareService -> Location) to be resolved in a single call.

The full list of applicable _includes are shown below. If any cannot be honoured the Receiver will respond, ignoring the unsupported _include(s), with the url reflecting this omission in the response Bundle.link.url.

|Expression                        | Inclusion         |Description|
|-------                           |--------           |-------- |
| Appointment:slot                 | Slot               | Include the Slot Resource(s) referenced within the Appointment Resources|
| Appointment:based-on             | ServiceRequest     | Include the ServiceRequest (referral) Resource that the Appointment is based on|
| Slot:schedule                    | Schedule           | Include Schedule Resources referenced within the Slot Resources|
| Schedule:actor:Practitioner      | Practitioner       | Include Practitioner Resources referenced within the Schedule Resources|
| Schedule:actor:PractitionerRole  | PractitionerRole   | Include PractitionerRole Resources referenced within the Schedule Resources|
| Schedule:actor:HealthcareService | HealthcareService  | Include HealthcareService Resources referenced within the Schedule Resources|
| HealthcareService:providedBy     | Organization       | Include Organization Resources referenced within the HealthcareService Resources|
| HealthcareService:location       | Location           | Include Location Resources referenced within the HealthcareService Resources|

**Example usage**

Get bookings for a patient and include just the Slot each booking is linked to:

`GET [base]/Appointment?patient:identifier=https://fhir.nhs.uk/Id/nhs-number|4857773456&_include=Appointment:slot`

Get bookings for a patient and resolve the chain from Slot through to the HealthcareService and Location it is delivered at:

`GET [base]/Appointment?patient:identifier=https://fhir.nhs.uk/Id/nhs-number|4857773456&_include=Appointment:slot&_include=Slot:schedule&_include=Schedule:actor:HealthcareService&_include=HealthcareService:location`

Get bookings for a patient and include the referral (ServiceRequest) each booking was based on:

`GET [base]/Appointment?patient:identifier=https://fhir.nhs.uk/Id/nhs-number|4857773456&_include=Appointment:based-on`

**Actor-based inclusions (Wayfinder Direct Integration compatibility)**

In addition to the BaRS reference chain above, the following actor-based shorthands are accepted. These resolve the resources referenced directly from `Appointment.participant.actor`, and are convenient when a Receiver models the Appointment's Location and Practitioner(s) as participants rather than via the Slot -> Schedule chain.

|Expression              | Inclusion                                   |Description|
|-------                 |--------                                     |-------- |
| Appointment:location   | Location                                    | Include the Location resource(s) referenced from `Appointment.participant.actor` (primarily to obtain the ODS code).|
| Appointment:actor      | Location, Practitioner, PractitionerRole    | Include all participant actor resources referenced from `Appointment.participant.actor`.|

Use `_include:iterate=PractitionerRole:practitioner` to additionally resolve the Practitioner referenced by an included PractitionerRole.

**Example usage (actor-based)**

Get a single appointment and include its Location:

`GET [base]/Appointment?_id=c3f6145e-1a26-4345-b3f2-dccbcba62049&_include=Appointment:location`

Get a single appointment and include all its participant actors, resolving the Practitioner behind each PractitionerRole:

`GET [base]/Appointment?_id=c3f6145e-1a26-4345-b3f2-dccbcba62049&_include=Appointment:actor&_include:iterate=PractitionerRole:practitioner`

AppointmentIncludeIterate_QParam.name: _include:iterate
AppointmentIncludeIterate_QParam.description: Requests an additional resource by following a reference from a resource already returned through `_include`. For example, when a PractitionerRole is included, use `PractitionerRole:practitioner` to include its referenced Practitioner in the same search Bundle. This parameter is optional and can be repeated when more than one iterative inclusion is supported.

AppointmentId_QParam.name: _id
AppointmentId_QParam.description:
The FHIR logical id of a single Appointment, supplied as a search parameter. Optional.

When provided, the search is constrained to the matching Appointment and returns it in a `searchset` Bundle (`total` 0 or 1), with any requested `_include` / `_include:iterate` resources included as additional `include` entries.

**`_id` (search) vs `GET /Appointment/{id}` (read) — which to use**

Both retrieve a single Appointment, but they differ in shape and capability:

* Use **`GET /Appointment/{id}`** for a straightforward read of one Appointment when you already hold its id and do not need related resources. It returns the Appointment resource directly (not wrapped in a Bundle) and is the simplest, most cacheable option. It does not support `_include`.
* Use **`GET /Appointment?_id=...`** when you want the single Appointment *together with* its referenced resources in one call, because search supports `_include` / `_include:iterate` whereas the read-by-id path does not. The result is a `searchset` Bundle (the Appointment as a `match` entry plus any `include` entries), so it is consistent with the patient-search response shape and lets a client use one Bundle-parsing path for both list and single-item retrieval.

In short: `/Appointment/{id}` for a plain read; `?_id=` when you need includes or a uniform Bundle response. Receivers that support search SHOULD support `_id`; a Receiver's supported interactions and `_include` values are advertised in its CapabilityStatement (`GET /metadata`).

4XX-BARS.description:
> **TODO — REVIEW REQUIRED:** This 4XX error catalogue is inherited from BaRS and needs review for the Direct Integration API. Reconcile the coded error list with the explicit 400/401/403 responses now defined (Unauthenticated, Forbidden, InvalidOrganisationHeader), confirm which codes apply to this API, and add any missing domain cases (e.g. 404 not-found, 429 rate limit, under-16 handling).

Below are examples of potential HTTP status codes and their associated error codes, which could be returned in the event of a fault. 
Guidance on error handling within BaRS can be found [here](https://simplifier.net/guide/nhsbookingandreferralstandard/Home/Core/1.4.0/Error-Handling).

The `Direct Integration` rows below are the codes surfaced by this API's dedicated response objects (`InvalidOrganisationHeader`, `Unauthenticated`, `Forbidden`). Where a status code appears both here and as a dedicated response, the **Notes** column flags the duplicate and states which definition is authoritative for that case.

| HTTP status | Source | Error code | Description | Notes |
| ----------- | ------ | ---------- | ----------- | ----- |
| 400 | Direct Integration | (OperationOutcome `required`) | Application-based request is missing or has a malformed `NHSD-End-User-Organisation` header. | **Authoritative for this API.** Served by the dedicated `InvalidOrganisationHeader` (400) response. **Duplicate 400** — see the two BaRS rows below; those are generic malformed-request cases, this is the specific org-header case. |
| 400 | BaRS | SEND_BAD_REQUEST | The API was unable to process the request. | **Duplicate 400.** Generic BaRS proxy case; overlaps with the Direct Integration 400 above. Review whether this applies to DI or is superseded by `InvalidOrganisationHeader`. |
| 400 | BaRS | REC_BAD_REQUEST | The Receiver has responded stating the message was malformed. | **Duplicate 400.** Receiver-side malformed case; distinct cause from the org-header 400 above. |
| 401 | Direct Integration | (OperationOutcome `login`) | Missing, invalid or expired API Platform access token. Returned with a `WWW-Authenticate: Bearer` challenge. | **Authoritative for this API.** Served by the dedicated `Unauthenticated` (401) response. **Duplicate 401** — supersedes the two BaRS 401 rows below for DI. |
| 401 | BaRS | SEND_UNAUTHORIZED | The API deemed you unauthorized to make this request. | **Duplicate 401.** Superseded by the Direct Integration 401 above. |
| 401 | BaRS | REC_UNAUTHORIZED | The receiver deemed you unauthorized to make request. | **Duplicate 401.** Superseded by the Direct Integration 401 above. |
| 403 | Direct Integration | (OperationOutcome `forbidden`) | Valid credentials but insufficient application permissions, organisation or patient access, or required patient identity assurance (P9). | **Authoritative for this API.** Served by the dedicated `Forbidden` (403) response. **Duplicate 403** — supersedes the BaRS 403 row below for DI. |
| 403 | BaRS | SEND_FORBIDDEN | Missing or Expired Token. | **Duplicate 403.** BaRS wording relates to token issues; for DI a missing/expired token is a 401 (`Unauthenticated`), and 403 is reserved for authorisation failures per the DI 403 above. |
| 403 | Direct Integration | UNDER_16_DENIED | The patient is under 16 years of age and is not permitted access to appointments via this patient-facing route. | **REVIEW REQUIRED.** Folded in from the Wayfinder standard. **Duplicate 403** — distinct cause from the authorisation `Forbidden` 403 above (this is an age-eligibility exclusion, not an auth-permission failure). Decision needed: keep as a `403 UNDER_16_DENIED`, or treat under-16 as a silent empty result (`200` `total: 0`) consistent with the PDS-sensitive / Trust-flag exclusions. Returning a distinct code discloses that an excluded record exists — confirm this is acceptable for a patient-facing API. |
| 404 | BaRS | PROXY_NOT_FOUND | No related people exist for given NHS number. |  |
| 404 | BaRS | REC_NOT_FOUND | Patient record for given NHS number has been invalidated and not superseded by another NHS number. |  |
| 405 | BaRS | SEND_METHOD_NOT_ALLOWED | HTTP Verb is not correct for this scenario. |  |
| 405 | BaRS | REC_METHOD_NOT_ALLOWED | Receiver does not allow this. |  |
| 405 | BaRS | PROXY_METHOD_NOT_ALLOWED | Proxy does not allow this. |  |
| 406 | BaRS | SEND_NOT_ACCEPTABLE | Senders message had an incorrect content type defined for a response. |  |
| 408 | BaRS | REC_TIMEOUT | The downstream domain processing has not completed within the configured timeout period. |  |
| 409 | BaRS | SEND_CONFLICT |  |  |
| 409 | BaRS | REC_CONFLICT |  |  |
| 409 | BaRS | PROXY_CONFLICT |  |  |
| 422 | BaRS | SEND_UNPROCESSABLE_ENTITY | Message was not malformed but deemed unprocessable. |  |
| 422 | BaRS | REC_UNPROCESSABLE_ENTITY | Message was not malformed but deemed unprocessable. |  |
| 422 | BaRS | PROXY_UNPROCESSABLE_ENTITY | Message was not malformed but deemed unprocessable. |  |
| 429 | BaRS | SEND_TOO_MANY_REQUESTS | The user has sent too many requests in a given amount of time |  |
| 429 | BaRS | REC_TOO_MANY_REQUESTS | The user has sent too many requests in a given amount of time |  |
| 200 | Direct Integration | (empty searchset) | Not an error. A successful search that matches no returnable appointments returns `200` with a FHIR searchset Bundle whose `total` is `0`. | **Included here for completeness of exclusion behaviour — this is a success, not a 4XX.** This same empty `200` `total: 0` response MUST be used when appointments are withheld by the exclusion rules (PDS sensitive/restricted, Trust-flagged patients, and — if the silent-exclusion option is chosen — under-16), so that a withheld record is indistinguishable from a patient who genuinely has no appointments and no exclusion is disclosed. **REVIEW REQUIRED** alongside the under-16 decision above. |

| HTTP status | Source | Error code | Description | Notes |

| 501 | BaRS | REC_NOT_IMPLEMENTED | The Receiver did not recognize the request. | May be used where a Receiver does not implement an optional interaction (e.g. create/update/patch/delete). Capability is advertised via `GET /metadata`. |

| 503 | BaRS | PROXY_UNAVAILABLE | The Proxy was unavailable to service the request. |  |
| 504 | Direct Integration | (Gateway Timeout) | The downstream Receiver did not respond within the gateway timeout. | **REVIEW REQUIRED.** Folded in from the Wayfinder standard. **Overlap** — BaRS models a downstream timeout as `408 REC_TIMEOUT` in the 4XX table; confirm which applies to this API (gateway `504` vs receiver `408`) and align, rather than defining both for the same condition. |

Appointment.description: FHIR Appointment resource for the appointment.

id.description: A GUID identifier for the appointment. It is preferable but not mandatory that this GUID links relationally to other resources in your system database.

meta.description: Metadata about the resource, including the FHIR profile(s) it claims conformance to and any security labels.

profile.description: The FHIR profile(s) this resource claims conformance to.

security.description: Security labels applied to the resource, for example a 'no disclosure to patient/subject' (NOPAT) confidentiality label.

contained.description: Inline resources referenced from within this Appointment, for example a Media resource referenced by the patient instruction.

items.description: A contained Media resource holding patient preparation guidance URL.

content.description: The actual content reference for the Media resource.

extension.description: FHIR extensions for the appointment resource.

anyOf.description: Appointment delivery channel - whether the visit is in person or remote (UK Core).

url.description: URI for the type of extension - in this case an appointment delivery channel.

anyOf.description: Appointment reschedule mode - whether the patient is allowed to reschedule the appointment (UK Core).

url.description: URI for the type of extension - in this case an appointment reschedule mode.

anyOf.description: Appointment cancellation mode - whether the patient is allowed to cancel the appointment (UK Core).

url.description: URI for the type of extension - in this case an appointment cancellation mode.

_patientInstruction.description: The FHIR R4 primitive extension sibling for the R5 `patientInstruction` element, carrying patient-facing instructions as a CodeableReference to a contained Media resource. Further information can be found in https://simplifier.net/packages/hl7.fhir.uv.xver-r5.r4/0.1.0/files/3366367/~overview

url.description: URI for the cross-version patientInstruction extension.

extension.description: The nested extension parts describing the datatype and the reference.

anyOf.description: Declares the datatype of the cross-version element.
The reference to the contained Media resource holding the instruction.

display.example: Arrive with a full bladder. Please review the preparation guidance before attending.

status.description: The appointment booking status as reported by the source system.

description.description: The patient-friendly standardised description/title of the appointment that would be appropriate to display to a patient.

specialty.description: NHS Specialty (UK Core practice setting code).

system.description: Coding system for the specialty / practice setting code.

start.description: Start date/time of appointment in a UTC format.

end.description: End date/time of appointment in a UTC format.

participant.description: Participants in the appointment, including the patient, practitioners, practitioner roles and the location. Each actor is expressed as a FHIR reference that can be resolved via `_include`.

reference.description: A relative reference to the participant resource, resolvable via `_include=Appointment:actor`.

display.description: A human-readable label for the participant.

slot.description: Slot(s) this appointment occupies. Resolvable via _include=Appointment:slot.

basedOn.description: The ServiceRequest (referral) this appointment is based on. Resolvable via _include=Appointment:based-on.

resource.description: A matched Appointment, or a resource pulled in via _include / _include:iterate.

RequestingOrganisation.title: NHSD-End-User-Organisation
RequestingOrganisation.description:
Requesting Organization described in an object based on a FHIR 'Organization' resource (Standard Base64 encoded JSON).
Different BaRS Applications may have different standards and requirements for the Access Control which these headers are used for. 

In this example an ODS code and the Organisation name is provided. Other identifiers are permitted if required.

RequestingPractitioner.title: NHSD-Requesting-Practitioner
RequestingPractitioner.description:
Requesting Practitioner described in an object based on a FHIR 'PractitionerRole' resource (Standard Base64 encoded JSON).

This item is not mandatory, however if the information is available it must be included in the request. Only in the event that it is not available, should it be omitted.

The example below shows a General Practitioner and their SDS Role profile Id.
The Base64 encoded example below shows a General Practitioner and their SDS Role profile Id.

RequestingSoftware.title: NHSD-Requesting-software
RequestingSoftware.description:
Requesting Software described in an object based on a FHIR 'Device' resource (Standard Base64 encoded JSON).
Different BaRS Applications may have different standards and requirements for the Access Control which these headers are used for. 

The identifier used here, though arbitrary, should be consistent across instances of a product, the name and version of the product should also be accurate and consistent.

Location.description: FHIR Location resource, included when `_include=Appointment:actor` resolves a Location participant.

name.description: Name of the location as used by humans.

position.description: The absolute geographic location of the Location, expressed using the WGS84 datum.

managingOrganization.description: The organisation responsible for appointment, identified by ODS code.

PractitionerRole.description: FHIR PractitionerRole resource, included when `_include=Appointment:actor` resolves a PractitionerRole participant.

code.description: Roles which this practitioner is authorised to perform for the organisation.

practitioner.description: Reference to the Practitioner who is in the role, resolvable via `_include:iterate=PractitionerRole:practitioner`.

Practitioner.description: FHIR Practitioner resource, included when `_include:iterate=PractitionerRole:practitioner` resolves the Practitioner referenced by an included PractitionerRole.

name.description: The name(s) associated with the practitioner.

given.description: Given names (not always first). Includes middle names.

NHSLoginPatientAccess.description: NHS API Platform access token obtained after NHS login authentication and token exchange. Accepted on all operations as an alternative to NHSApplicationAccess; patient-level authorisation applies. See Security and authentication in the API overview. OpenAPI 3.0 has no native token-exchange flow, so this scheme describes the bearer credential presented to this API.

NHSApplicationAccess.description: NHS API Platform access token obtained using OAuth 2.0 client credentials with a signed JWT client assertion. Accepted on all operations as an alternative to NHSLoginPatientAccess. NHSD-End-User-Organisation MUST be supplied and validated against the authenticated application. Application and organisation permissions apply. This scheme describes the bearer credential sent to the API; acquire the token using the documented signed-assertion flow.
